title: Set-lintegrals agree when sets and integrands agree on a null-measurable set off which both sets are null
statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N; μ need not be σ-finite. Let G ⊆ ℝ^N be μ-null-measurable, and let D, D' ⊆ ℝ^N be arbitrary sets with μ(D ∖ G) = 0 and μ(D' ∖ G) = 0. Suppose that for every x ∈ G, x ∈ D ⟺ x ∈ D'. Let f, g : ℝ^N → [0,∞] be arbitrary functions with f(x) = g(x) for every x ∈ G. Then ∫⁻_D f dμ = ∫⁻_{D'} g dμ.
lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (G D D' : Set (Euclidean N)) (f g : Euclidean N → ℝ≥0∞), NullMeasurableSet G μ → μ (D \ G) = 0 → μ (D' \ G) = 0 → (∀ x ∈ G, x ∈ D ↔ x ∈ D') → (∀ x ∈ G, f x = g x) → ∫⁻ x in D, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in D', g x ∂μ
